_readme: Verbatim review copies of official MOEX ISS responses used to verify the cross-venue basis
normalisation on 2026-09-22 (the previous session's blocker). These copies were retrieved
through the review platform's page fetcher on 2026-09-22 during the working session; the
engine re-fetches the same endpoints itself in every tick and records the authoritative
SHA-256 of each response it receives (data/history/moex-ref/{SECID}.json, plus the
description_source_url / description_source_sha256 fields on each instrument).
What these establish, from the exchange's own machine-readable reference data:
GDZ6 (GOLD-12.26):     LOTSIZE=1,  UNIT=USD, FACEUNIT=USD, EXECTYPE=cash-settled
SVZ6 (SILV-12.26):     LOTSIZE=10, UNIT=USD, FACEUNIT=USD, EXECTYPE=cash-settled
PTZ6 (PLT-12.26):      LOTSIZE=1,  UNIT=USD, FACEUNIT=USD, EXECTYPE=cash-settled
i.e. the MOEX quote is USD per unit of the underlying with the stated lot size, which is
exactly the normalisation the cross-venue basis strategy was missing before 2026-09-22.
Kalshi's side of the normalisation is the `contract_size` field of the official Perps API
(gold 0.001, silver 0.1, platinum 0.001 oz per traded unit), documented in the Kalshi help
centre's perp contract specification (help.kalshi.com article 15357587).
Cross-venue sanity check on 2026-09-22 22:23Z (both venues' own payloads, same run):
Gold:   Kalshi KXGOLDPERP mid 4.36325 / 0.001 = 4363.25 USD/oz  vs MOEX GDZ6 mid 4433.25  (+1.6% MOEX premium)
Silver: Kalshi KXSILVERPERP mid 6.72255 / 0.1 = 67.2255 USD/oz vs MOEX SVZ6 mid 68.36   (+1.7% MOEX premium)
Two independent regulated venues within ~2% of each other corroborates the unit chain; a
lot-vs-unit or gram-vs-ounce error would produce a 10x or ~32x gap instead.
note_on_palladium: The MOEX FORTS listing verified 2026-09-22 contains no palladium asset code (the P codes are PLT/PLTM platinum and PLD/PLDM/PLZLM equities), so no cross-venue palladium pair exists and none is traded.
